rationale: Read the third receipt (execution b6089b103bbb467199d051f4492e82c8, exit 0, both cases passed): with every comparison scoped by tag all five now evaluate completely and hold, so the starvation mechanism is decided on a clean comparison set - repeated snapshot installs on a fixed snapshot index, the follower not reaching the cluster frontier, and the stale cached claim persisting, with the untrimmed control negative on both count and progress. With the account decided, the next judgment-changing actions are the two limits it still states: whether the monotonic-store branch (delete-all-logs on install) stalls the same way, and whether the stall ends only once a snapshot above the follower's cached claim is published. The harness now covers both as additional cases, and this update records the decided interpretation and requests those two cases as the successor experiment.

interpretations.rationale: Present conclusion: a follower that accepts an InstallSnapshot whose index does not exceed its own cached last log index is left advertising a log it no longer holds; it then fails every prev-log check from that leader and accepts no further log entry, while the leader retries the same snapshot over and over. Source basis: installSnapshot sets lastApplied, lastSnapshot and the configurations but never lastLog (src_install_snapshot_tail, raft.go 1837-1977, tail at 1952-1977); getLastEntry prefers the cached log tail whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex (src_get_last_entry, state.go 160-174); prev-log verification then misses below the log store's first index or mismatches the stale suffix (src_append_prev_check, raft.go 1458-1606); the leader can only walk nextIndex down one step per rejection (src_replicate_failure, replication.go 240-300) until setupAppendEntries reports ErrLogNotFound, which jumps to SEND_SNAP and, on acceptance, resets nextIndex to snapshotIndex+1 (src_send_snapshot_result, replication.go 352-372); the non-monotonic compaction path keeps any suffix above the snapshot index while the monotonic branch deletes the whole store without resetting the cached claim (src_compaction, snapshot.go 217-279). Decided execution evidence (execution b6089b103bbb467199d051f4492e82c8, version 3, exit 0, both cases passed): the trimmed setup event (index 0) records the restarted follower's cached claim at (98, term 2) with the leader's snapshot at 83/term 3 and its store 1-98 intact; the trimmed probe (index 14) records the follower's FSM restored 5 -> 1255 times in the 3s window with the leader's snapshot index unchanged at 83 (comparison 0 holds), its applied index unchanged at 83 while the cluster frontier reached 95 with new entries applied elsewhere (comparison 1 holds), the cached claim still (98, term 2) with the store suffix 84-98 kept (comparison 2 holds), its commit index still 0, and one stable leader set with the follower's term fixed at 3. The untrimmed control on the same history (setup index 15, probe index 29) records no accepted snapshot and full repair by entries (comparisons 3 and 4 hold), so the install path together with the trimmed leader log, not the stale suffix itself, is the trigger. Two earlier receipts of the same family (5e63769a85ac4b5f90ebe12a4ddcc5fd, d1897256143f4de2b0477a3460ae392b) show the same signature with the follower's claim drifting in step with its orphan suffix (95-105), which is why the numbers differ between runs while the predicates do not. Limits and the pending boundary probes: the stall is expected to end only when the leader publishes a snapshot whose index exceeds the follower's cached claim, because then getLastEntry stops preferring the stale tail; nothing in these runs produced such a snapshot (automatic snapshotting was disabled and the leader's last index stayed below the claim), so the account claims starvation for as long as the leader re-ships a snapshot at or below the claim, not permanent starvation. The monotonic-store branch is likewise expected to stall because the store is emptied while the claim survives; both expectations are the current discriminator and are now covered by the requested successor cases rather than by any retained receipt. Local construction runs of those two cases behaved as predicted (monotonic: restores 5 -> 1283 with applied fixed at 83 and the store empty, claim persisting; repair: after the stall the leader's applied index was driven past the claim of 96 and a snapshot at 97 was published, after which the follower applied 83 -> 108 and its claim became (108, term 3)), but those are construction feedback, not retained evidence. Remaining unmeasured: the vote-side consequence of a stale claim (a voter that rejects a candidate whose real log is ahead), larger clusters, longer windows, other TrailingLogs values, and a production BoltDB-style monotonic store (this experiment uses the in-process test wrapper).
counterevidence: The untrimmed control accepted no snapshot, repaired the stale suffix with ordinary log entries and reached the cluster frontier, so a stale suffix alone does not stall replication; the trimmed leader log together with the install path is the trigger.

A successful InstallSnapshot refreshes the follower's last contact, so the follower never campaigned: every receipt in this family shows one stable leader set for the whole window and the follower's term fixed, so the starved state is stable rather than self-healing by election.

The starved state is bounded in principle: a snapshot whose index exceeds the follower's cached claim would restore getLastEntry consistency. No run produced one because automatic snapshotting was disabled and the leader's last index stayed below the claim, so this account claims starvation only while the leader keeps re-shipping a snapshot at or below the claim.

The first two runs' comparisons resolved unknown for harness reasons (a missing mode field, then missing applicability scoping), not because the observation failed; the third run's complete comparison set supersedes them for the verdict while both receipts keep their own raw values.
limitations: Measured configuration only: three voters, InmemStore plus FileSnapshotStore, TrailingLogs=10 against a large control, an idle cluster with one write per 250ms sample, a 3s window and a single induced full partition of one voter.
The monotonic-store behaviour and the recovery boundary are source-derived and only locally probed; their retained receipts are pending in the requested successor.
The vote-side consequence of the stale claim is source-derived and unmeasured; no election was induced while the follower held the claim.
The follower's commit index was never advanced by the install path (0 while applied was 83) and is reported as an advertised-state inconsistency rather than as an independent defect.

scope.description: Two new cases of the same three-voter history, each built on the unchanged scenario (isolated leader appends entries that never reach a quorum, is shut down, remaining voters elect a leader, commit further entries and take a snapshot, isolated node restarted on its real log store and reconnected). Case one repeats the trimmed configuration with a MonotonicLogStore so the install path deletes the whole log store instead of keeping a suffix above the snapshot index. Case two keeps the non-monotonic store and, once the stall is established, drives the leader's applied index past the follower's cached claim and publishes a snapshot above it, then keeps sampling to see whether the follower resumes accepting entries.
assumptions: Fault model unchanged: no message loss inside the injected transport; the only induced events are a full transport partition of one voter, its clean shutdown and restart on the same stores, and in case two additional client writes plus one forced snapshot on the leader.

Case one uses the captured MockMonotonicLogStore wrapper over InmemStore (IsMonotonic true), so installSnapshot takes the removeOldLogs branch; the leader's own snapshot trimming still uses compactLogs, as in the earlier runs.
Case two adds only: entries applied on the leader until its applied index exceeds the follower's cached claim, then one forced Snapshot(); the stall is measured before those additions.

Reused facilities otherwise unchanged: MakeClusterCustom/MakeClusterOpts with inmemConfig timings, InmemStore, FileSnapshotStore, InmemTransport, MockFSM wrapped by a counting Restore, and the NewRaft restart pattern used by TestRaft_SnapshotRestore_Progress.
excluded: No production logic was modified; the harness only adds test code.
Automatic snapshotting remains disabled (SnapshotThreshold huge, SnapshotInterval 1h) so the leader's snapshot index is controlled by explicit calls in both cases.

experiment.prefix: Same scenario driver as the earlier revisions, now parameterised by log-store monotonicity and by an optional repair step. Case one: the trimmed history runs with MonotonicLogs=true; the follower's install deletes its entire log store, and the probe reports whether installs repeat, whether the follower reaches the frontier, whether the cached claim persists, and whether any suffix above the snapshot index survived in the store. Case two: the trimmed history runs as before; when the sample loop passes 1200ms it records the pre-repair applied index, restore count and cluster frontier, keeps applying entries on the leader until its applied index exceeds the follower's cached claim, forces Snapshot() and records the new snapshot index, then continues sampling to 4s and reports whether the stall was present before the repair and whether the follower caught up afterwards.
semantic_changes: The scenario driver gained a monotonic-store parameter and an optional repair step; the two new cases use them, and only those two cases are selected for this run.
Two new comparison subjects are recorded: the monotonic case's emptied log store with a persisting claim, and the repair case's stall-then-recovery boundary.
experiment.requirement: A follower that reinstalls the leader's snapshot must remain able to accept subsequent log entries from that leader, or its cached log state must not claim entries the snapshot superseded.

comparisons.description: Monotonic store: the follower's FSM was restored again after the first install, i.e. the same snapshot index was re-shipped during the window with the leader's snapshot index unchanged.
Monotonic store progress predicate: after the window the follower's applied index is still below the cluster frontier although new entries committed and applied elsewhere.
Monotonic store: the follower's cached last log index is still at or beyond the installed snapshot index with a lower term.

Monotonic store: the install branch deleted the whole log store, so no entry above the snapshot index survived, while the cached claim above it persisted - the distinction from the non-monotonic case.
Repair boundary: before the intervention the follower's applied index was below the cluster frontier while repeated restores were being recorded, i.e. the stall was already present.

Repair boundary: after the leader committed past the follower's cached claim and published a snapshot above it, the follower's applied index reached the cluster frontier again, so the stall ends at the claim boundary rather than being permanent.

experiment.revision_reason: The third run decided the original five comparisons (all complete and hold), so the harness now covers the two limits that account still states instead of repeating those cases: a monotonic-store variant of the trimmed case, and a repair-boundary case that publishes a snapshot above the follower's cached claim after the stall is established. The scenario driver, stores, restart technique and the earlier cases are kept in the file but only the two new cases are selected for this run; the earlier receipts remain the evidence for the non-monotonic trimmed and control cases.
